PASS for the exact partial mathematical task. I independently checked the round73 proof, n1–n3, and n4’s mathematical gap analysis. This does not establish the original P13.2 image characterization or higher-dimensional existence. The previous review was not used as a theorem. Operational and preservation claims were excluded.

The full P13.1 mathematical body is used exactly as task-granted background and is therefore excluded from the external-premises list. Its applicable scope includes the actual classes, fixed carrier, calibrated rational quotient, positive same-field products, integration by parts, mixed Hodge seminegativity, weighted decreasing-net continuity, root bijections, and outer differentiation. No envelope attainment, strong completeness, inverse existence, or cross-Reeb mixed calculus is added.

Normalization is consistent. The rational reference product model gives the trivial-valuation Dirac probability; the granted radial calibration and bounded irrational passage preserve it. Thus normalized potentials satisfy u(v_triv)=sup_K u=0 and J(u)=−E(u). The factors V_eta=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(L_d^p), omega_eta^p=sV_eta, E_eta=E_Ld/(sd), and E=(n+1)S/n are retained. Every new polynomial pairing keeps V^(−1) and dd^c rho^+.

The finite-target criterion is established. For bounded-above usc functions on compact Hausdorff K, Radon regularity gives the integral as the infimum of continuous-majorant integrals, including extended values by truncation. Compactness and directedness make a continuous majorant plus epsilon eventually dominate a decreasing net. Consequently decreasing target integrals converge without metrizability. Uniform FS approximation identifies the FS and CPSH suprema; decreasing energy and target-integral continuity establish E1 integrability when L is finite and identify the E1 dual supremum with L.

The converse also works. If negative target integration were unbounded on normalized J≤1, the weighted convex partial sums would decrease to an actual nontrivial PSH potential with energy at least −1 and infinite negative target integral. Closure under this decreasing passage follows from the actual definitions and compactness: continuous strict majorants can be refined downward using a sufficiently late PSH member and then a sufficiently late continuous defining approximant. No envelope theorem is required. The segment expansion has b_0=0 and gives J(tu)≤2^n t²J(u). Optimizing −J+B+B√(2^nJ) gives exactly L≤B+2^(n−2)B². The granted onto-E1 root bounds then transport this target class on the same K.

The concave tangent inequality has the correct sign. Raw decreasing approximation passes it to E1 and gives L(MA(u))=E(u)−∫u dMA(u). Both signs of outer differentiation give the error d_u/s+C_f s. Density and probability mass one prove weak convergence of genuine maximizing FS outputs. This works for every maximizing sequence or net: fix s, let the deficit vanish, then let s vanish. Deficit zero implies the equation only for an already actual potential.

The midpoint calculation is correct. Its Green kernel is (1/2)min(t,1−t); restricting to [1/4,3/4] gives the valid lower constant a_p=p/4^(p+1). Hence I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p) and J(u)≤I(u,0)≤(d_u+L)/(2a_p). Each passage to E1 uses finite combinations of granted weighted mixed integrals. Maximizing potentials are I-Cauchy. The Hodge estimate (22) follows from Q_j(f)≤2A||f|| and finite Cauchy–Schwarz. An actual E1 I-limit would realize the target; existence of that limit remains an antecedent.

The fixed-ray polynomial is genuinely linear and well defined. A relation among restrictions extends to the identical relation among zero-slope extensions. Signed products therefore do not depend on presentations. Every direction in the CPSH span is a positive multiple of a difference of two actual CPSH restrictions, by splitting coefficients and padding both positive combinations with the reference. For a positive cone slot, Omega_(s,d)=s dd^c(rho+d_tilde/s); a boundary constant slot has zero curvature. The granted mixed Hodge inequality consequently establishes quadratic positivity for every kernel direction and every positive remaining slot.

Expanding the energy gives H(1,u)=E(u), using binom(p,l)/(l+1)=binom(p+1,l+1)/(p+1). Integration by parts gives ∂_dH[f]=V^(−1)∫f Omega^p dd^c rho^+. Two derivatives contribute −p, while polarization contributes (p+1)p, confirming the factor −1/(p+1). The positive deficit expansion gives I/(p+1)≤delta≤pI/(p+1), delta+delta_reverse=I, and delta(u,0)=J(u). These verify the exact Appendix A hypotheses; nonlinear roots are not treated as linear forms.

I opened [2307.01697v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.01697v1) and checked the applicable statements and proof bodies. The interpolation recurrence retains √(b_jB). Convexity controls the auxiliary midpoint distance before the quasi-triangle inequality is proved. Absorption supplies a dimension-dependent constant, after which averaging positive slots and Cauchy–Schwarz give the mixed and derivative estimates. With the source dimension equal to p, the exponent is alpha=2^(−p). For p=1 this reduces directly to quadratic Cauchy–Schwarz. This establishes (33) on continuous actual potentials; raw weighted decreasing approximation, followed by subtraction of convergent normalization constants, extends it to E1.

The unbounded target limit has the correct order. Fix a continuous defining approximant of phi, first send the maximizing output measures to mu, and only then send the potential net to phi. The fixed target uses the established target integrability; the fixed MA(psi) uses granted weighted continuity. With B0=1+(L+1)/(2a_p), this proves exactly |∫phi d(MA(psi)−mu)|≤C_p√d_psi J(phi)^alpha(J(phi)+J(psi)+B0)^(1/2−alpha). It gives (35), uniform signed convergence on bounded-J sets, including B=0. The genuine tangent identity then gives (36), convergence of output dual energies. Comparing outputs with the reference gives (37); maximizing-sequence target integrals and normalized energies are Cauchy and have finite limits. These statements do not establish absolute L1 continuity for arbitrary weak, nonmonotone potential nets.

The elementary supports are valid at infinite coordinates. Supported coefficients are positive and have sum less than one, so every nonzero finite-coordinate recession direction has positive cost. Bounded difference sublevels confine supported coordinates and bound the remaining coordinates below; compactness then gives the strict gap outside any contact neighborhood. The empty supported set is included. Multinomial maxima have the claimed uniform error throughout the extended product. Rational rounding and separated epsilon levels make the approximants decrease. Terms beta_i=1, beta_0=m−1 retain the original generators themselves.

The pole-sensitive approximation is also correct. The bounds F_ij≤D_iH and epsilon_j−epsilon_(j+1)≥ΣD_i(q_i,j+1−q_ij) prove monotonicity. Domination follows from epsilon_j≥ΣD_i(p_i−q_ij), H≥0, and the logarithmic upper bounds, including negative logarithms. A positive lower multiple of H permits original-generator branches to be appended without changing each finite maximum. At a supported pole the pointwise limit is −infinity. This proves decreasing approximation by actual AFS presentations, without asserting membership in the source’s inconsistent printed lower-growth subclass. The pertinent definitions were checked in [2609.27610v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1).

The normal localization implication retains its entire antecedent (42). Divisor rays give orders of the actual rational functions. For q/r>c/a, all height-one orders of h^r f^q are nonnegative, and the normal-domain intersection property in the granted body places that element in the original A. The original-ring hull inequality gives 2a(q/r)M; decreasing rational ratios give exactly 2cM. Vanishing cases avoid subtraction of infinities. Controlled approximation of a weak localized input is not inferred.

The retraction lemma is valid without openness: inverse images of carrier neighborhoods give one usc inequality, and restriction of ambient neighborhoods gives the other. Rational carrier-envelope membership retains the independently proved projective EP antecedent. On the torified product K×R, uniform orbit slopes and action homeomorphisms give both raw-root identities, including roots equal to −infinity. Thus carrier membership transports after a base exists, without transporting completeness or strong topology.

The mathematical gap analysis is sound. The squared positive logarithm is locally psh by decreasing rational secants, satisfies the printed lower-growth condition, and cannot admit a first global AFS majorant because its Gauss-ray growth is quadratic. This refutes the printed lower-growth formulation, not a corrected upper-growth theorem. The final envelope proof explicitly depends on the weak/global chain. The disconnected-trace objection is concrete: for z↦z², use base residue disks around 1 and 4, selecting both inverse disks over 1 and only the positive inverse disk over 4. The trace is respectively two and one. Continuity therefore establishes only local constancy; gamma=1 also needs separate treatment. These rejected bridges are not premises of the retained conclusions. The full synthetic theorem concerns measure completeness and supplies no actual E1 realization here. The projective variational comparison was also checked against [1801.08229v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4), without applying its existence theorem to the cone.

For n=1, the granted effective normal grading gives R=k[z], K={v_triv}, E(c)=c, and the sole probability. Realization modulo constants is immediate; the p≥1 estimates are not applied with a_0. Harmless precisions are to choose positive rational lower coefficients q_ij, or discard an initial tail; interpret uniformly upper-bounded equivariant families on K; retain dimension-dependent implicit constants in Appendix A; and interpret zero exponents as one. No substantive repair is needed.

premises: Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:2307.01697v1, Appendix A: let p≥1, π:V→Θ be a surjective real-linear map, F:V→R a homogeneous polynomial of degree p+1 with symmetric polarization, and P⊂V a convex cone satisfying a²·x₂···x_p≥0 for every a∈kerπ and x_i∈P. On a fixed fiber P_θ, set δ(x,y)=F(x)−F(y)−⟨F′(y),x−y⟩. Then δ is nonnegative, quasi-symmetric, and satisfies a quasi-triangle inequality; F and δ(·,y) are convex on that fiber. For x_*,x_i,y_i,z_j∈P_θ, α=2^(−p), and M=max_ζδ(ζ,x_*) over the points appearing in the respective left-hand side, |(x₀−y₀)(x₁−y₁)z₂···z_p|≤C_pδ(x₀,y₀)^αδ(x₁,y₁)^αM^(1−2α), and |⟨F′(x₀)−F′(y₀),x₁−y₁⟩|≤C_pδ(x₀,y₀)^(1/2)δ(x₁,y₁)^αM^(1/2−α). Constants depend only on p; zero exponents are interpreted as one.

Lyuhui Wu, arXiv:2609.27610v1, Definitions 3.1, 3.8 and 3.15: tropical affine functions are real-valued and continuous, with every coefficient-times-coordinate finite on their charts; rational tropical PL functions use finite open covers and finitely many rational affine branches. Local psh functions are generically finite, usc, and locally pointwise decreasing-sequence limits of tropically convex rational PL functions. On an affine variety Y over the non-Archimedean field K, an affine FS function is max_i{c_i log|f_i|+C_i,λ}, where c_i are positive rational numbers, C_i and λ are rational, and the f_i generate K[Y]. Printed logarithmic growth means g≤u+O(1) for some global affine FS g; regularizability in that printed class means pointwise decreasing approximation by global affine FS functions.

Its proof claims an upper FS growth bound and invokes Lemma 3.25(1). That lemma explicitly retains the hypotheses of Proposition 3.17(1), additionally assumes u∈PSH_log,reg(Y^an), assumes u≤g+O(1), and takes c>1 before asserting psh membership of u−cg extended by −∞ outside Y.

The printed Theorems 6.3 and 6.5 require a complete discretely or trivially valued equicharacteristic-zero field with a countable dense subfield; Theorem 6.5 concerns a projective variety with a semipositive form of ample underlying class, and its proof invokes Theorem 6.3. Its arbitrary-field proof descends finite data and individual PL competitors to countable fields and invokes contact orthogonality, exact MA pushforward compatibility, and domination over a larger countable field.
